title: Comparatives 4: Short Forms (выше, ниже, дальше, дешевле, старше, шире)
titleRussian: Сравнительная степень 4: Короткие формы (выше, ниже, дальше, дешевле, старше, шире)
description: Six very common comparatives drop part of their adjective and become short one-word forms: высокий → выше, низкий → ниже, далёкий → дальше, дешёвый → дешевле, старый → старше, широкий → шире. Today you learn to recognise and use these six.
descriptionRussian: Шесть очень частых сравнительных форм теряют часть прилагательного и становятся короткими: высокий → выше, низкий → ниже, далёкий → дальше, дешёвый → дешевле, старый → старше, широкий → шире.
intro: Six more that refuse the regular ending, and this group carries a specific trap. The forms you would build by rule do not exist in Russian at all, so a learner who has just mastered lesson 1 will confidently produce a word no Russian has ever said. Tall, low, far, cheap, older, wider: these six have to be known, not worked out.
rules: Six common comparatives are short forms: высокий → выше, низкий → ниже, далёкий → дальше, дешёвый → дешевле, старый → старше, широкий → шире. Learn each one directly.
Do not add -ее to the full adjective. Высокее and дешёвее do not exist; the correct words are выше and дешевле.
Дешевле is the odd one: it ends in -ле, while the other five end in -ше or -е (выше, ниже, дальше, старше, шире).
These short forms never change their ending. Выше stays выше for any subject: Антон выше, Лена выше, гора выше.
examples: Эта башня выше, чем дом. (This tower is taller than the house.) высокий → выше.
Полка ниже окна. (The shelf is lower than the window.) низкий → ниже.
Школа дальше, чем магазин. (The school is farther than the store.) далёкий → дальше.
Чай дешевле кофе. (Tea is cheaper than coffee.) дешёвый → дешевле; note the -ле ending.
Антон старше сестры. (Anton is older than his sister.) старый → старше, used for people.
Эта дорога шире, чем та. (This road is wider than that one.) широкий → шире.

items.promptEnglish: This tower is taller than the house.
items.hint: Short comparative of высокий. What is left after the word gets shorter?
items.explanation: Выше is the short comparative of высокий: the word gets shorter, and you learn the short form directly.

items.hint: This is the odd one in the group. It ends in -ле.
items.explanation: Дешевле is the short comparative of дешёвый, and it is special because it ends in -ле.

items.promptEnglish: The shelf is lower than the window.
items.hint: Short comparative of низкий. The opposite of выше.
items.explanation: Ниже is the short comparative of низкий, the opposite of выше.

items.promptEnglish: The school is farther than the store.
items.hint: Short comparative of далёкий / далеко. Think of 'go farther'.
items.explanation: Дальше is the short comparative of далёкий / далеко, meaning 'farther'.

items.prompt: Антон _____ своей сестры на два года.
items.promptEnglish: Anton is two years older than his sister.
items.hint: Short comparative of старый, used for people.
items.explanation: Старше is the short comparative of старый and is the normal word for people ('older').

items.promptEnglish: The new road is wider than the old one.
items.explanation: Шире is the short comparative of широкий ('wider'); you learn the short form directly.

blanks: Эта куртка _____ , чем та. (This jacket is cheaper than that one.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Дешевле is the short comparative of дешёвый, and it is the odd one in the group because it ends in -ле.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This mountain is taller than that one.
errorCorrection.explanation: Высокий has the short comparative выше. The form высокее comes from adding -ее to the full word and is not real Russian; this is exactly the trap of today's lesson.
The short comparative of дешёвый is дешевле, the one that ends in -ле. Дешёвее adds -ее to the full word and does not exist.

errorCorrection.sentence: Брат старее меня на три года.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My brother is three years older than me.
errorCorrection.explanation: For a person's age the short comparative of старый is старше. Старее is not used for people.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This river is wider than that one.
errorCorrection.explanation: Широкий has the short comparative шире. Широкее adds -ее to the full word and is not real Russian.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The store is farther than the house.
minimalPairs.explanation: Дальше is the short comparative ('farther'). Далёкий is the plain adjective ('far'), not a comparison. The comparison 'X is farther than Y' needs the short word дальше.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This window is lower than the door.
minimalPairs.explanation: Ниже is the short comparative ('lower'). Низкое is the plain adjective ('low') in the neuter, not a comparison. To say one thing is lower than another, use the short word ниже.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This wardrobe is taller than that one.
minimalPairs.explanation: Выше is the short comparative ('taller'). Высокий is the plain adjective ('tall'), not a comparison. The comparison needs the short word выше.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each word: is it a plain adjective, or a short comparative from today's set of six?

sentenceBuilding.translation: This house is taller than the school.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Use the short comparative выше. Start with 'этот дом'.
Use the short comparative дешевле (the one that ends in -ле).

sentenceBuilding.translation: The sister is older than the brother.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Use the short comparative старше, the normal word for a person's age.

reviewVocab.definition: taller, higher / lower (short comparatives of высокий and низкий; the ending never changes)
reviewVocab.example: Башня выше дома, а полка ниже окна.

reviewVocab.definition: cheaper (short comparative of дешёвый; the odd one, ending in -ле)
farther / older (for people) / wider (short comparatives of далёкий, старый, широкий)
reviewVocab.example: Школа дальше магазина, а Антон старше сестры.
